replacement.limits: Static teaching freeze only: no speed, reach, interception timing or uniquely optimal route is validated. Answers are coaching suggestions grounded in visible cues.

questions.prompt: Where are YOU relative to W?

options.text: Below W near the end line
Above W at the point
Behind Gold 1 at centre ice

questions.explanation: Your location creates the low cycle option; moving level with W changes that relationship.

questions.prompt: Which two relationships help a low cycle?

options.text: A low lane below wall pressure
D2 staying high enough to balance
W and YOU must both drop below the goal line

questions.explanation: The low lane moves the puck away from pressure while D2 balances above; crowding removes the next option.

questions.prompt: Order one low-cycle support check.

options.text: See whether W can protect the puck
Present below pressure
Reassess D2’s high balance

questions.explanation: W’s control decides whether a cycle exists; low support gives a release; checking D2 prevents an exposed point.

questions.prompt: Move YOU below and inside W to show a low cycle option.
questions.explanation: The lower-inside spot gives W a short route away from Gold 1 and keeps the net-side lane visible; if Gold 2 drops, move higher.

questions.prompt: If Gold 2 drops below W, what should YOU reconsider?

options.text: Whether the low lane is still open or higher support is safer
Cycling into Gold 2 because the puck is nearby
Leaving D2 with no balance

questions.explanation: Gold 2’s drop changes the low lane, so read coverage before moving; if it stays open, keep it available without forcing.

questions.prompt: What must W see before using your low option?
questions.explanation: W needs your separation from Gold 2 and a reachable lane without a blind pass; if pressure closes it, protect and wait for D2.

reasons.issue: W (n2), the puck carrier, is described in the briefing and cues as being 'on the right half wall,' but the setup placed W at (x=22, y=2) - about 10.95m from the nearest side boards (boundary ~=12.95 at that x), i.e. near mid-ice width rather than the boards. Every other 'half wall' scene in the 200-scenario snapshot places its puck-side carrier at |y|~=6-10 (e.g. exp26b-u13-013's Gold 1 at y=-8, exp26-u11-013's F2 at y=8, exp26b-u15-002's YOU at y=9), so y=2 is a clear outlier. The mismatch also makes q4's own claim numerically false: q4 asks to place YOU 'below and inside W' at reference (24,8), but with W at y=2, |8| is not less than |2|, so the reference sits farther from centre ice than W - outside W, not inside.
reasons.change: Moved W (n2) from (22,2) to (22,9) - matching the bank's own half-wall convention and sitting just inside the offensive-zone faceoff circle near the boards, consistent with Gold 1 'fronting the wall' from (24,4) (now positioned between W and the middle of the ice, which is what 'fronting' the wall means). Recomputed the carried-puck point from the documented formula (x=actor.x+cos(facing)-0.7*sin(facing), y=actor.y+sin(facing)+0.7*cos(facing)) using the unchanged facing=2.9, giving puck=(20.8616, 8.5596). No actor label, team, role, or question option/answer text was changed by this fix alone; it also makes q4's 'below and inside' claim numerically true.
reasons.evidence: Computed with the project's own tooling (validation/src/one-on-one/coachRouteSurfaceInput.js isCoachRoutePoint plus a corner-boundary distance function, and validation/tools/question-batch-core.mjs questionContentHash / validation/src/one-on-one/experimentalBankCore.js validateExperimentalBank): original W at (22,2) is 10.954m from the boards; after the fix, W at (22,9) is 3.954m from the boards and 2.642m from the offensive-zone faceoff-circle centre (20.7,6.7) given in the project instructions, matching the |y|~=6-10 band used by 18 other 'half wall' scenes surveyed across bank-snapshot.json. q4's reference (24,8): |8|<|2| is false before the fix (not inside W); |8|<|9| is true after the fix (inside W). validateExperimentalBank([replacement]) returns zero errors; makeScene(replacement).puck remains on the ice (isCoachRoutePoint true).

sourceChecks.scope: WebFetch's text extraction failed (scanned/image-heavy PDF); read the saved binary directly with the Read tool's PDF-page-image extraction, pages 12-18. Pages 12-13 (Breakouts) cover retrievals, support, passing and protecting the puck under pressure. Pages 14-15 (Neutral Zone Regroups) explicitly name 'D-D open ice reverse' and 'D-D hinge' as team regroup options and instruct 'read puck possession quality when supporting your D partner.' Pages 16-17 cover neutral-zone defend; page 18 covers shooting. Supports the reverse-read (exp26b-u13-001) and hinge-support (exp26b-u13-002) teaching concepts and the general principle of reading pressure/support before choosing an outlet. Does not certify the exact coordinates, guaranteed outcomes, or a single correct route in either scenario; original coaching synthesis built on the stated principle, consistent with the source's own 'use' disclosure.
